# Conference Abstract — Version 5

Purpose: describe the conference talk after integrating “The AI Path to Mars.”

## The Intelligence Layer for Mars

Mars will not be settled by intelligence alone. It will be settled by teams that convert intelligence into reliable, verifiable and accountable physical action. Mars exploration and settlement combine planetary science, aerospace engineering, robotics, life support, propulsion, power, construction and operations in decisions constrained by mass, energy, schedule and communications delay. The practical bottleneck is the path from uncertain evidence to an approved engineering result.

This presentation proposes a staged Mars Harness rather than a single model or chatbot. The model supplies intelligence; the harness supplies mission capability through orchestration, instructions, tools, context, memory, specialist agents, validation and approval. Specialized harnesses Discover, Engineer, Verify, Deliver and Evolve through explicit work products and ground-truth gates. Every claim carries an epistemic status—Observed, Derived, Assumed or Unknown—while provenance separately records whether its source is literature, simulation, test or field observation. Consequential actions require human approval.

Hypatia Pro structures scientific discovery through falsifiable questions, evidence grounding, explicit variables, experiments and simulations, statistical inference and adversarial critique. Intelligent Engineer Pro converts approved evidence and unresolved uncertainty into phase-gated requirements, trades, designs, DFMA/FMEA, verification plans and controlled releases. Durable mission memory preserves evidence, provenance, configuration state, decisions, dissent and lessons learned across people, tools and model generations.

A Mars ISRU case study begins with NASA’s MOXIE result: 16 oxygen-producing runs, 122 grams of oxygen, a most-efficient rate of 12 grams per hour and product purity of at least 98 percent. Those facts establish feasibility, not habitat-scale readiness. The harness turns the remaining gaps—continuous duty cycle, stack life, dust tolerance, storage and maintenance—into traceable requirements and a bounded research request. The architecture extends to rovers, habitats, advanced propulsion, power, agriculture, medicine, construction and complex program coordination. Eight platform-neutral skill blueprints make the pattern portable across Codex, Claude Cowork, Hermes, Gemini, Grok and future governed runtimes.

## Short program description

Bob J Mills presents a practical Mars Harness that converts model intelligence into verified mission capability. The talk links science, physical engineering, verification, delivery and field learning through explicit evidence status, human approval and durable mission memory, using MOXIE scale-up as a concrete case study.

## Keywords

Mars; agentic AI; engineering; scientific discovery; ISRU; MOXIE; verification; mission memory; human approval; autonomous systems; settlement.

## Version 5 emphasis

The talk now follows a complete arc: science → engineering → build → operations. It explains the expanded harness architecture, durable skills and agent identities, explicit epistemic status, structured evidence handoffs, bounded research returns, verification from the first claim, compounding mission memory, Mars-local autonomy, the MOXIE-to-settlement-scale case study, portable runtime skills, and a one-loop adoption strategy.
